title: The Stillson
notes: At the oversized Stillson in the get-in. Taking it is a commitment: it never enters the case, so from here it is dragged until it is set down. The refusal is not a dead end — the wrench stays where it is and can be taken later.

lines.text: A Stillson nearly two metres long, laid across the maintenance rack with the jaw hanging off the end of it.
That is not a tool, that is a fixture. Somebody bolted this building together with it.
It comes up off the rack about a foot and stops. Both hands, and it is still going down at one end.
No. It does not go in the case and it does not go on a shoulder.
It goes on the floor, behind me, all the way down. And every foot of that is a noise.

choices.text: put it back and find the small one

lines.text: Right. Handle in both hands, jaw behind me, and do not stop on the stairs.
It goes back across the rack with the jaw hanging off the end of it, where it has been since the works.
There will be a spanner in this building somewhere. There always is.
